measure.measure_definition: Occurrence: achieving ACR20 response at Week 12; Participants; American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 20 composite assessment at baseline and Week 12: tender and swollen joint counts of 28 joints (scale 0=best to 28=worst) plus 3 of 5 measures: HAQ-DI (0=no difficulty to 3=unable to do), subject global assessment (0=best to 10=worst), subject pain (0=no pain to 10=worst), evaluator's global assessment (0=best to 10=worst), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) concentration (mg/L).; Response defined as at least 20% improvement from baseline to Week 12 in tender and swollen joint counts of 28 joints and in 3 of the 5 listed measures. The primary endpoint uses baseline at the day of consent; the separate ACR20 endpoint referenced to day-0 randomization is excluded.

Occurrence: achieving EULAR good or moderate DAS28-CRP response at Week 12; Participants; DAS28-CRP calculated from tender and swollen joint counts of 28 joints (scale 0=best to 28=worst), subject global assessment (0=best to 10=worst), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP, mg/L): DAS28-CRP = 0.56*sqrt(TJC28) + 0.28*sqrt(SJC28) + 0.36*ln(CRP+1) + 0.014*SGA + 0.96. Assessed at baseline and Week 12.; EULAR good or moderate response: moderate if DAS28-CRP improvement from baseline to Week 12 is >0.6 and <=1.2 with Week 12 DAS28-CRP <=5.1, OR improvement is >1.2 with Week 12 DAS28-CRP >3.2; good if improvement is >1.2 with Week 12 DAS28-CRP <=3.2. This measure captures the combined good-or-moderate category as reported.
measure.measure_name: DAS28-CRP EULAR good or moderate response

measure.measure_definition: Blinded month-three HAQ-DI response referenced to consent baseline. A decrease of 0.22 points is the reported meaningful improvement criterion. The inequality boundary is unspecified. The 20 items cover eight functional areas. Each area uses its highest item score, raised to 2 for use of aids, devices or assistance if the score is 0 or 1. The overall 0–3 score averages the scored areas when at least six are available. Lower values indicate less disability.
